speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: After a full day of discussing racial harmony and social cohesion, I think this Adjournment Motion topic on addressing discrimination does appear to parallel much of what we deliberated and segue quite nicely to the end of the Parliamentary day.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It can be confronting to our own biases, shine light on our unconscious prejudices and it tends to be a topic that needs to be tread sensitively at times.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Amidst the diversity of our own backgrounds, ethnicities, cultures, upbringing and life experiences, all of us have blind spots and shortcomings relative to the view of others around us.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: On that basis, all of us also consider different positions because we are indeed varied and diverse ourselves.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: At other times, we may disagree and vehemently so.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: However, we must continue to be active in reaching out to the others, especially if they are different, take effort to know them well and make a genuine attempt to build trust amidst our differences.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Pandering to reductionist stereotypes, painting a group or community with a broad brush and dismissing negative experiences as an exception rather than a lived reality, can funnel us towards a worldview that is unjust, prejudicial and ignorant.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We must protect our society against discrimination if we want to continue to be a society that is cohesive and one of high trust.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: This is a step in the right direction, but the debate over the Bill also brought up a few key points.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Often, the root of any discriminatory view would have been seeded much earlier in a person.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It arises from a broad-based societal view that informs how we see our neighbours, our classmates, our colleagues and people who are different from us.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Though the characteristics are already broadly scoped and covers most groups, it is more important that we, as a society, develop a genuine willingness to appreciate diversity of individuals in our midst and possess a readiness to see them for their strengths, rather than focus on the differences along the lines of the said characteristics.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: And thirdly, not all decisions that go against a particular individual or a group are a function of discrimination and injustice.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In the context of the workplace, it is necessarily a competitive hiring process and employers have to take a view that considers their business needs as well.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Protected characteristics aside, really, the spirit of such decisions must be underpinned by fairness and transparency in the hiring process, benchmarked against ability and value proposition of the prospective employee.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Similarly, in any society, especially one as diverse and multicultural as ours, I think it is important to acknowledge in this Adjournment Motion that not all decisions will always be in one's favour and where they are not, they are not necessarily a function of discrimination, per se.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: How then do we stem discrimination more effectively?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, we do want to celebrate our differences; our respective traditions, our heritage and cultures; they mean a lot to us.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We also want to harmonise our rich diversity and we want to draw collective strength from all backgrounds, perspectives and ideas.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: With these differences, however, there will be some tension and propensity to recognise that we are not the same, that we, too, are filled with our own biases and sometimes, prejudice can rear its ugly head.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Certainly, discrimination is not something we can sweep under the carpet nor pretend that it is not there.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: As a society, I think we do reasonably in balancing this, compared to many other parts of the world that is filled with much polarity and prejudice today.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Our efforts to expose our young to the varied life experiences of others, whether they be of individuals with disability or special needs, of different races, religions and cultures, or of different age groups and caregiving roles must start in school.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I now wish that when I was in school, I had met someone like my learned and hon friend, and fellow Nominated Member of Parliament, Mr Ong Hua Han, earlier.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Not at a cursory hi-bye level, but really to get past any initial awkwardness and have a meaningful conversation and friendship at depth, to learn more about his view of the world from the chair that he sits and appreciate better the genuine struggles that I may have taken for granted.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: My view is that if more of our students have the opportunity for such exchanges with people who are different from their own lived experiences, their ability to challenge their own stereotypes will change more easily and society will be better for it in time.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Among others, this could be related to disability, mental health, racial or religious identity, language, nationality or different socio-economic status.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: On this note, I also wonder if there is scope to improve the opportunity for growth and leadership for minorities and the disabled in our schools.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: How many head prefects have there been in our schools where it came from someone who was a minority or disabled?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Can one imagine a student in a wheelchair, notwithstanding his or her physical limitations, but with an inspiring leadership ability to also be the class chairman?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: If there was a younger version of Singapore's most decorated Paralympian and former Nominated Member of Parliament, Ms Yip Pin Xiu, could or would she be considered as her school's swim captain or part of the leadership committee of her co-curricular activity?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Second, we can and must do better in telling more stories of success and challenge more robustly discriminatory narratives.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We must empower minorities and marginalised groups through mentorship and guide them to seize readily available opportunities.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We should make attempt to amplify their success stories to challenge any negative stereotypes that present a false view of their actual potential and ability.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: This is because role models are powerful and important to inspire others and to open up pathways to help people believe that they too can do it.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: When one starts from a position of being discriminated against and representation from that particular group is limited at the onset, the tide can only turn when we facilitate examples of success and affirm our stand as a society, through lived examples and stories, that discrimination is not okay.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: First, it gives an example and confidence to those at the margins and from minorities that they too can succeed.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Whether we would like to admit it or not, what discrimination does is that, over time, it suppresses and pigeonholes groups to a diminished role rather than allow them to flourish and fulfil their real and true potential.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Stories can be powerful in breaking that mindset, especially among those who hesitate not for their lack of ability, but for a lack of self-esteem and confidence in themselves.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Second, when we tell enough of such stories of success, it reminds the remaining majority to confront any long-held discriminatory biases that do not hold true.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Third, we should strive for more common spaces that allow broad-based interactions and reduce opportunity for marginalisation of any particular group.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Could we encourage more sports and common activities where disability matters less or does not matter at all to the outcome of the activity?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: If I had a go at e-sports or a game of chess with my hon friend, we would see ourselves as equal in the game.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, I may not stand a chance.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It is the case that for sports, specifically, the Paralympics, as a movement, has been an enabler for inclusivity and participation for those with specific impairments.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: However, I think we could do more to promote activities where everyone has an equal and good chance at enjoying and succeeding in that activity without concern of a handicap or a differential ability.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It gives us room and space to also have conversations and experience one another as equals.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: This is something I think we can do better to explore.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Additionally, for traditional and cultural-based events, the practical and honest truth is that, more often than not, it is championed by participants of the same ethnic or cultural community.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: By an overwhelming majority, it is likely that in activities, such as the Chinese Orchestra, Silat, Sepak Takraw or Indian dance, it is participated by specific groups of individuals.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: So, could we encourage more cross-cultural participation in our schools or community activities and challenge the urge to silo these activities within a narrow band of participation?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Is there any way to better foster diversity in participation and encourage a wider inclusion for such activities?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Fourth, beyond the workplace, it is important that we strengthen efforts to address any gaps in our legislature and policies.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In the last Sitting, we discussed workplace fairness; and in this Parliamentary Sitting, we also discuss issues related to racial harmony and how we will not allow nor tolerate discriminatory behaviours or actions of hatred and ill will on the basis of race, to take root in our society.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We also have parallel laws for religious harmony today.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Beyond the law, perhaps, it would be helpful to also look at other sectoral practices with potential smirks of discriminatory practice as well.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: For example, how can we better improve the state of insurance policies for individuals who are disabled or inflicted with mental health conditions?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It has been the case that the Government has been forthcoming towards greater representation of minority communities and marginalised groups, but I think we can do more.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I am sure the examples I share will require more study but in the spirit of wanting to aspire to remove discrimination entirely, I think the examples that follow are worth some thought.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: First, imagine how the worldview of a young student can be shaped and informed, for the better, in my opinion, if inclusive hiring practices and accessibility support is available in our schools such that it allows even for a wheelchair-bound principal or teacher to educate comfortably in our classrooms?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Or how stereotypes are challenged when a teacher from a minority community teaches the second language of the majority in Mandarin, or vice versa?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I would venture that this is not a far-fetched idea where remote technology, cybersecurity and digital systems form a strong part of our defence and security strategy, and not all tasks require the full extent of physical ability.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: If this were possible, would that not signal to others about our seriousness to be a cohesive and inclusive society and how important the institution of National Service is for us as a symbol of universality and collective unity as a people?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Third and finally, it bears considering how widely representative and diverse the leadership at all levels of our Public Service is today.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Is there a lack of representation in certain sectors and can we do better?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: If there is a lack, I think it is important to study this and to find ways on how we can encourage more broad-based participation from minorities or groups at the margins so that there is access to a diversity of views for decisions taken in Public Service.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: When hiring and representation is broad-based and inclusive, then there is also opportunity for greater diversity in leadership to emerge from the Public Service.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We are products of different experiences and surely, we want to be able to celebrate our own unique identities and cultural backgrounds.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: However, it should not be that we ever allow ourselves to divide as a result of that difference.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We should not allow our blind spots and stereotypes to propagate discriminatory practices due to our ignorance of the other.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We may prefer sameness and familiarity in our comfort zones, but we must also recognise that there is strength in diversity and a richness to that.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Most paintings, Mr Speaker, are beautiful because there is much diversity and a celebration in the conglomerate of colours that make up the painting.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Even in monochrome colours, a skilled artist plays with a variety of tones and textures.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It takes skill, a lot of work and training to flow and blend the different parts of a painting to achieve the beautiful end result.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This Government is committed to working with partners to combat discrimination and to build an inclusive society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It is underpinned by the principle of non-discrimination.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our Constitution provides that all persons are equal before the law and entitled to equal protection of the law.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have a strong legal framework, including the Penal Code and the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act, to deter any attempts at undermining our racial and religious harmony.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have laws that foster an inclusive society for minority groups, such as persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Second, we implement policies that foster social integration and protect the interests of minorities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: One example is our Ethnic Integration Policy in public housing estates, which ensures a balanced mix of residents from different ethnic groups.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through our schools, we build a shared Singapore identity from an early age, yet preserving our diverse cultural heritage.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Regardless of race, language or religion, we sing our national anthem, recite our national pledge and study the national curriculum.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We all learn English so that we can have a common lingua franca and learn our mother tongue to preserve each ethnic group's cultural heritage.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: There are also dedicated efforts to improve the inclusion of persons with disabilities and persons with mental health conditions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Enabling Masterplan 2030 is our national roadmap to build a more inclusive society for persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And the National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy launched two years ago in 2023 promotes mental health and well-being in our families, communities and workplaces.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Dr Syed Harun had mentioned insurance as a specific area where persons with disabilities and persons with mental health conditions face challenges.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Regardless of pre-existing conditions or disabilities, we ensure that all Singaporeans have universal basic health insurance coverage under MediShield Life and younger Singaporeans also have long-term care insurance under CareShield Life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore also updated its Guidelines on Fair Dealing last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Insurers must assess every application, including from persons with disabilities and persons with mental health conditions, based on reliable information and data that is relevant to the risks being insured.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Third, we are committed to enlarging the common spaces in which all Singaporeans live, work and play.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In schools, we nurture values such as empathy and respect in a diverse student population that learns, plays and grows up together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The importance of racial and religious harmony, awareness about disabilities and mental health conditions, are taught in Social Studies, and Character and Citizenship Education curricula, as well as school activities and programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: All schools organise learning journeys to cultural and heritage sites, celebrate cultural festivals to help students to hone racial and religious sensitivities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Schools also promote a culture where students are sensitive to the needs of others, including peers with special educational needs (SEN) or disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Ministry of Education and Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth also ensure that leadership opportunities within and outside schools are open to our youth who show potential, regardless of their background.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: At the workplace, beyond the Workplace Fairness Legislation and the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices, we will press on with education efforts to grow the mindset – that everyone benefits from a fairer and more inclusive workplace.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Public Service does not tolerate any form of workplace discrimination and harassment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Public agencies have also adopted the Tripartite Standards for Flexible Work Arrangements to provide flexibility for officers, including those with disabilities or additional caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Eight public agencies have achieved the Enabling Mark certification for disability-inclusive hiring, including VITAL as well as the National Library Board which have achieved the highest tier, the Enabling Mark Platinum.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Public Service values a diversity of perspectives, experiences and capabilities in its leadership teams and commits to reaching out to a diverse range of candidates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In our communities, there are Racial and Religious Harmony Circles in every constituency.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They bring leaders from different ethnic and religious communities together to organise activities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We also have dedicated efforts to raise awareness and encourage inclusion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SG Enable’s i’mable movement seeks to raise disability awareness through efforts, such as the "UnAwkward" campaign.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They also partner the community through the Well-Being Circles under the SG Mental Well-Being Network.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And finally, we harness the power of sports and the arts to bring people together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In sport, we are building up a network of world-class sporting infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have also created diverse and inclusive sports programmes for different groups of Singaporeans to pursue their sporting interests.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In the arts, we are expanding arts accessibility and inclusivity to bring people of different backgrounds and abilities together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our cultural institutions, like museums provide inclusive spaces and programming for all.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I visited the Punggol Regional Library a while ago and I am sure it is a fine example of a truly inclusive space that embraces visitors of all abilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On a related note, the President’s Challenge has similarly been refreshed to support such projects that uplifts those with less in life as well as to help those pursuing second chances.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: True inclusion requires each of us to rethink the stories we tell.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Last year, I was invited to watch a showcase titled “Theatre for Dreams” at the Esplanade.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Under the guidance of artist-facilitator Oniatta Effendi and her team, young men from the Singapore Boys’ Home – crafted scenes inspired by their very own personal stories, struggles as well as reflections.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They told stories about their hope and dreams and aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Not stories about their limitations and they were not merely subjects of their stories.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They were their own story-tellers and their stories were powerful and moving.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: So, each of us can shape positive narratives that build a more inclusive society – by being story-tellers of the aspirational Singapore that we want to live in.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Therefore, I thank Member Dr Syed Harun for moving this Adjournment Motion, for giving us a chance to see that combating discrimination is not something that we can take for granted or leave to chance.
